title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: f is an automorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space V of dimension n (more generally a virtual or graded object). Then ε(f) is the rank, or Euler–Poincaré characteristic, and det f is the alternating determinant. Write P_f(t) = det(1 - f t) = ∏(1 - λ_i t), where λ_i are the eigenvalues. The contragredient f̌ (the transpose inverse acting on the dual V^∨) has eigenvalues λ_i^{-1}. The page computes:

P_{f̌}(t) = ∏(1 - λ_i^{-1} t) = ∏ λ_i^{-1}(λ_i - t) = ∏(-λ_i^{-1} t)(1 - λ_i t^{-1}) = ((-1)^n t^n / det f) · P_f(t^{-1}).

It then boxes the result in the form valid for virtual objects:

P_{f̌}(t) = (-t)^{ε(f)} (det f)^{-1} P_f(t^{-1}).

Equivalently, with L_f = 1/P_f:

L_{f̌}(t) = (-t)^{-ε(f)} det f · L_f(t^{-1}).

This is the linear-algebra core of the functional equation of geometric L-functions. In the cohomological setting, Poincaré duality identifies H^{2d-i} with the contragredient of H^i (up to a Tate twist), and multiplicativity over the graded pieces then gives Z(1/(q^d t)) = ± q^{dχ/2} t^χ Z(t). That is the subject of cote 60.

The heavily abbreviated French remark that follows seems to be a caveat. The formula involving t^{-1} only makes sense because P_f is a polynomial; it is not meaningful for P_f(t) taken as an arbitrary formal power series. The point that the products obtained, computed as formal series, are actually polynomials (rationality) is a genuine result, and the earlier condition was only needed in that case. The final sentences are largely illegible.
errors: No mathematical error. The struck-out intermediate line carried both (-1)^n t^n and ε(f) at once, a slip that was corrected in the boxed formula.
The sign and exponent conventions are consistent: P_{f̌}(t) = (-t)^{ε} det(f)^{-1} P_f(1/t) and, for L = 1/P, L_{f̌}(t) = (-t)^{-ε} det(f) L_f(1/t). Both check out.

ideas.what: Relation between the characteristic polynomial of an automorphism and that of its contragredient: P_{f̌}(t) = (-t)^{ε(f)} det(f)^{-1} P_f(t^{-1}), extended to virtual or graded objects via ε = Euler characteristic and alternating determinant.
ideas.modern_name: Reciprocal polynomial identity; linear-algebra step in the functional equation of zeta/L-functions via Poincaré duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical linear algebra; its use for the functional equation goes back to Weil's conjectures and is standard in the Grothendieck school (Grothendieck's Bourbaki talk on the Lefschetz formula and rationality, SGA 4½ 'Rapport', SGA 5)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L', Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 279 (1964), and the SGA 5 discussion of the functional equation; also Deligne's SGA 4½

ideas.what: Caveat that the substitution t -> t^{-1} requires P_f to be a polynomial, not an arbitrary formal power series; rationality is a theorem about the formal series.
ideas.modern_name: Rationality of the L-function as a prerequisite for stating the functional equation

deep.surprise_reason: Standard elementary computation (determinant of the contragredient) used as a lemma toward the functional equation of geometric L-functions. It is well documented in Grothendieck's published work and in SGA 4½/SGA 5. There is nothing new.
